exposure: Pregnancy in women with epidermolysis bullosa (EB)
outcome: Patient-reported symptoms and complications during pregnancy
cohort: This study assessed 33 pregnancies in 19 women with epidermolysis bullosa encompassing all major EB subtypes, classified by individual overall EB phenotype (mild, moderate, severe) prior to pregnancy.
finding: Pregnancy management in women with epidermolysis bullosa is feasible, though antenatal and perinatal complication rates tend to rise with increasing disease severity.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was the predominant mode of birth (67%) and appears to be a viable option, while caesarean section rates increased with EB severity (0% in mild, 38% in moderate, and 50% in severe EB groups).
